rows.what the ink shows: The baseline has one x, a circled cross, and one y with a descending tail beneath a clear long overline. Two separate dense, hooked strokes lie immediately above x and y; their overlap does not determine whether the inner bars remain or were cancelled.

Two heavy diagonal strokes cross between barred E and barred F, with a distinct curved enclosure still visible below and at the left. The overlapping strokes do not determine whether the enclosure belongs to the retained sign or is a cancelled remnant.

The rotated marginal word begins with a low connected loop group followed by an ascender, then a tall crossed medial stroke, a dot, and a low terminal run. These support application despite the diagonal cancellation crossing the middle.

A marginal l-like upstroke, dotted i and compressed low continuation support linéaire, but the nested cancelled span is crossed by a heavy horizontal line and two diagonal strokes. The visible upper word and lower cancelled remnants do not fix the source placement or all middle letters securely.

Before the period and the tall looped P of Par, the marginal word consists of an initial low rising stroke, a long compressed horizontal middle and a final small hook. These are compatible with norme, but do not separate its internal letters sufficiently to remove uncertainty.

The parentheses enclose a y with a long descender, a comma and a crossed x, without indices or powers. A dense irregular raised stroke spans the letter pair; the visible overlap does not decide whether it is a retained overline or a cancelled one.

The word immediately before the obscured middle cluster has a tall f with a lower loop, a low joined ai stroke, and a sharply crossed terminal t. The f and terminal t agree with the uncanceled fait later on this page; a separate short canceled word precedes it.

Between fait and the barred E, low separated humps and a right-hand dot remain below an upper retraced cancellation. The two long cancellation strokes mask the letter bodies and do not permit a secure two-word recovery.

After the barred E, the deleted span retains a few low humps, a loop dropping beneath the cancellation, and a later tall upright. Almost all connecting letter bodies coincide with the two deletion lines, so the three words cannot be distinguished securely.

Below the insertion, the canceled word retains a looped initial d-like stroke and a tall f with a lower loop. The thick horizontal cancellation covers the accent and remaining low letters, so définie remains plausible but not fully demonstrable.

The small interlinear word above the deleted band begins with an open e, continues through angular low n/c strokes and a rounded o, then a short r join and closed terminal e. It is separate from the cancellation and has no tall initial d or f.

The canceled word below the insertion has an initial dot and short upright, several mid-word tops, and a late raised stem and dot. The heavy descending strike conceals the o/m bodies and most of the ending; it supports the proposed isométrie only incompletely.

The inserted first word has two short low humps followed by a tall l and an explicit stop, supporting appl. The second begins with a tall b and dotted i/j strokes; its following strokes descend into the cancellation and do not securely distinguish the full ending from an abbreviation.

A short d-like ascender appears at the left, with a taller hooked f-like stroke farther right. Two heavy cancellation rules hide the intervening letters and any cedilla, so the complete proposed words remain uncertain.

The left part of the upper deleted strip preserves shallow arches and small uprights, but the rule passes through their joins; an oblique remnant crosses the middle. These remnants do not securely distinguish the proposed muni de la or its word boundaries.

The right part of this strip has a d-like ascender followed by a raised point, then a taller looped group crossing the rule. The cancellation conceals their connections, leaving neither a secure word reading nor a secure boundary with the preceding marked words.

The lower deleted strip begins with a hooked stroke descending below the rule, compatible with f, and a later small loop rises above it. The interior strokes of the proposed forme de are merged into the heavy rule and are not individually recoverable.

Farther along the same rule there are two short upright or dotted remnants and a pronounced tall loop with a descender, followed by low ink islands. Their connecting strokes are covered, so no reliable sequence or word count can be recovered.
